blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: Primary carnitine deficiency due to SLC22A5 loss of function — SLC22A5 encodes the high-affinity OCTN2 carnitine transporter. Loss of OCTN2 impairs cellular carnitine uptake and renal carnitine reabsorption, causing very low plasma and intracellular carnitine and limiting transport of long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria for beta-oxidation.
blueprint.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
blueprint.exact_outline_path_verification: Pending direct comparison with official outline; not certified by this screen.

distractor_explanations.A: Incorrect. Carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase moves acylcarnitines across the inner mitochondrial membrane after cellular carnitine has already been acquired; it is encoded by SLC25A20, not SLC22A5.
distractor_explanations.B: Incorrect. CPT I catalyzes formation of acylcarnitine on the outer mitochondrial membrane and is not the SLC22A5-encoded transport step.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. SLC22A5 encodes OCTN2, the high-affinity carnitine transporter responsible for cellular uptake and renal conservation of carnitine. distractor_explanations.A: Incorrect. A reciprocal PMP22-containing duplication at this locus is associated with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1A rather than HNPP.
distractor_explanations.B: Incorrect. Neuronal sodium-channel gain-of-function causes channelopathies such as some epilepsy or pain syndromes, not the recurrent pressure palsy phenotype produced by PMP22 deletion.
distractor_explanations.C: Incorrect. Dystrophin deficiency causes Duchenne/Becker muscular dystrophy rather than a compression-sensitive demyelinating neuropathy.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. HNPP is a PMP22 dosage disorder. The recurrent 17p11.2 deletion produces PMP22 haploinsufficiency, reducing peripheral myelin protein 22 and predisposing nerves to focal demyelination after pressure.
distractor_explanations.E: Incorrect. MFN2 dysfunction is associated with axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth neuropathy and is not the molecular consequence of the PMP22 deletion shown.

item.vignette: A 27-year-old man has had several episodes of transient foot drop and hand numbness after prolonged leg crossing or leaning on his elbows. His father has a similar history. Nerve conduction studies show a demyelinating peripheral neuropathy, and chromosomal microarray identifies a recurrent deletion at 17p11.2 involving PMP22.
